documents.title: Glucagon kit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Cleaning out my bag and realized my glucagon kit expired in November. I've never used it. Can you send a new one or do I need to go through endo? Same pharmacy as always.

documents.title: RE: Glucagon kit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Good catch. Since endocrinology manages your insulin and the kit, I called their office and they're sending a new glucagon kit to your pharmacy today. If it isn't there by tomorrow afternoon, message us back and we'll chase it.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Date of visit: 09/10/2024
Re: Abigail Lemieux, DOB 10/08/1999

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Lemieux for her scheduled follow-up of type 1 diabetes. She has used basal-bolus insulin for five years now and control remains good: her most recent A1c is 6.8%. No hypoglycemic episodes since her last visit.

Current regimen: insulin glargine 20 units subcutaneously at bedtime; insulin aspart 8 units subcutaneously before meals; glucagon 1 mg IM emergency kit on hand.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: maternal aunt with Hashimoto thyroiditis; paternal grandfather with type 2 diabetes.
Social: graduate student, never smoker, drinks rarely. She is a committed runner and is about to start marathon training, with daily runs that will go beyond an hour.

Her main question today was how to handle insulin and food once the long runs start.

Vitals within normal limits. Examination unremarkable.

Assessment and plan:
Type 1 diabetes, well controlled. Doses unchanged. We went through exercise planning in detail: check glucose before she sets out, periodically during any run longer than an hour, and again afterward and at bedtime on long-run days; carry fast-acting carbohydrate on every run; she may take a smaller aspart dose with the meal before a long run, using her own judgment and her logs. Late lows after long runs were discussed.
Return in 6 months.

With thanks,
Outside endocrinology group

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, rescheduled from 9/17. Turns 25 next week.

Diabetes: endocrinology letter from 9/10 in, A1c 6.8, no lows, doses unchanged (glargine 20 qhs, aspart 8 AC, glucagon kit). She has started marathon training and is following the plan endo gave her: checks before and after long runs, gels in her pocket, trims the pre-run aspart a bit. No lows so far. Eye exam with her optometrist this summer, told no changes; report not received yet.

Fall 2023 endo note never arrived despite our request in April; the new letter covers it.

No new symptoms. NKDA. SH: never smoker, rare alcohol.

ROS negative.
PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lean, well. HEENT and neck normal. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix normal, Pap obtained. Feet: intact skin, pulses full, monofilament and vibration normal. Neuro normal.

A/P
1. Type 1 diabetes: well controlled per endo. Yearly CMP, lipids, TSH, urine microalbumin drawn.
2. Running: no issues; reviewed staying hydrated and the late-low risk endo raised.
3. Cervical screening: Pap today, three years after 2021.
4. Flu and COVID given today.
5. Back next fall.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Abigail, blood work from Tuesday is all normal: kidneys, liver, cholesterol, thyroid and urine protein. Pap result usually takes about a week, I'll send it when it's in. Good luck with the training.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap came back normal. Next one in three years, fall 2027.
